manifest.route_capture: modal_app.py::capture_routes (exact noaux_tc recompute from checkpoint gate weights: sqrtsoftplus, bias-for-selection-only, norm_topk_prob, scale 1.5)

decode_regime.note: meaningful cross-position locality at K=1; predictive caching viable for autoregressive decode

wide_verification_regime.note: per-block unique-expert working set exceeds any VRAM budget by >10x; even Belady cannot help because the objects within a single wide block are mostly unique

notes: Objects are (layer, expert): an expert's weights in different layers are distinct tensors.
Belady = farthest-next-use eviction (max-heap via negated key); strict hierarchy: VRAM eviction demotes to RAM, RAM eviction to NVMe.
Metrics separate VRAM-resident (no transfer) / RAM-sourced H2D / NVMe-sourced bytes.
Stall uses provisional transport (H2D 12 GB/s, NVMe 3.5 GB/s); Phase 2.12 replaces with measured values.
63-position corpus limits K56 to 1 block/prompt; K<=16 gives more blocks and more stable per-block statistics.

The wide-K collapse is structural: at K=56 each block touches ~3800 unique expert-layer objects (~50 GB packed4); a 4 GiB cache holds ~300. No cache policy can bridge a 10x working-set gap. Residency for wide verification must come from reducing bytes (compression, representation) or accepting the bandwidth cost (Dual-Rail), not from smarter caching.
